name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
description: Counteracts climbing grip and desk-work tightness.
instructions_excerpt: Extend one arm in front with palm up. With the other hand, gently pull the fingers back toward the body, stretching the forearm flexors. Hold 20-30 seconds per side. Repeat 2-3 rounds.

name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
description: Stretches the forearm extensors — counterpart to the flexor stretch.
instructions_excerpt: Extend one arm in front with palm down. With the other hand gently press the back of the hand down and toward the body. Hold 20-30 seconds per side.

name: Forearm Self-Massage
description: Soft-tissue work on flexors and extensors — post-climb recovery staple.
instructions_excerpt: Rest the forearm on a table. Use the opposite thumb or a lacrosse ball to apply sustained pressure to tight spots on the forearm flexors (palm side) and extensors (back side). Work from elbow toward wrist. 2 minutes per side.

name: Finger Glides
description: Low-intensity tendon gliding — post-climbing finger recovery.
instructions_excerpt: Move each finger through: straight → hook fist → straight fist → straight → tabletop → straight. 5 slow reps per finger. Do both hands.

name: Active Hang / Shoulder Decompression
description: Light loaded hang with active engagement — restorative for pulled shoulders.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings on a sturdy jug. Actively engage the shoulders (no passive hang). Hold 20-30 seconds, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 times.

name: Walking (Low-Intensity Zone 2)
description: Low-impact aerobic recovery — the most undervalued recovery tool.
instructions_excerpt: Walk at a pace where conversation is comfortable but steady (Zone 2, ~60-70% max HR). 20-45 minutes on flat or gently rolling terrain.

name: Arm Swings (Warm-up)
description: Dynamic shoulder warm-up — ranges the shoulder in every plane.
instructions_excerpt: Stand tall. Swing both arms forward in large circles for 10-15 reps. Reverse for 10-15 reps. Then swing across the body (hug yourself). Then up-and-down.

name: Leg Swings (Warm-up)
description: Dynamic hip and leg warm-up — multi-planar range-of-motion flow.
instructions_excerpt: Stand next to a wall for balance. Swing one leg forward and back 10-15 times. Then swing side-to-side across the body. Switch legs.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Reach
description: Neuromuscular control — ankle stability and hip control.
instructions_excerpt: Stand on one leg, slight knee bend. Reach forward, then across, then back with the other leg while maintaining balance. 3 reaches per direction; switch sides.

name: Banded Shoulder Dislocation (Warmup)
description: Dynamic shoulder mobility drill — critical for swim stroke entry position.
instructions_excerpt: Hold a band (or PVC) wide overhead. Slowly rotate the band from in front of the body, overhead, and behind (keeping arms straight), then reverse. Move through the full shoulder ROM.

name: Wrist Wrestling Hold (Partner or Band)
description: Isometric wrist/forearm battle against band or partner — trains the wrist rotational strength used in grip fighting.
instructions_excerpt: Anchor a band to a post at wrist height, or partner up. Grip the band/partner hand in a thumb-up position. Resist rotation in both directions for 10-15 seconds each. 3-4 bouts per wrist.

name: Forearm Self-Massage (Grappler)
description: Targeted self-massage of forearm flexors/extensors — resolves post-gi or post-sparring forearm pump.
instructions_excerpt: Sit and place one forearm on the opposite thigh. Use the heel of the other hand or a massage ball to work slowly up and down the forearm flexors and extensors. Spend 2-3 minutes per arm.

name: Hip 90/90 Breathing Flow
description: Seated 90/90 hip position with paced breathing — recovery mobility for the court-athlete hip.
instructions_excerpt: Sit on the floor with one leg 90° in front (shin parallel to hips) and the other leg 90° to the side. Inhale 4s, exhale 6s. Hold 5-8 breaths. Rotate through the hips to swap sides (a "windshield wiper"). Continue 2-3 minutes.

name: Forearm Trigger Point Release
description: Targeted self-myofascial release on the forearm flexors and extensors — essential recovery for the tennis-elbow-prone racquet player.
instructions_excerpt: Using a lacrosse ball against a desk or wall (or a massage gun), press into the meat of the forearm. Slowly roll and pause on tight spots for 20-30 seconds. Cover both flexor (palm-side) and extensor (back-of-hand-side) compartments. 2-3 min per arm.

name: Shoulder Distraction Hang
description: Passive hang for shoulder decompression — the single best recovery tool for paddle-sore shoulders.
instructions_excerpt: Hang from a pull-up bar with relaxed shoulders (let the shoulders shrug up). Breathe. 20-45 seconds per hang.

name: Hollow-to-Arch Rock
description: Transition between hollow and arch — gymnastics warm-up staple.
instructions_excerpt: Start in hollow body. Roll to prone and into arch body position. Roll back to hollow. Maintain tension throughout each position.

name: Turn-Prep Pirouette Drill
description: Pirouette passé prep — stand on single leg in relevé with the other foot at the knee.
instructions_excerpt: Start in fourth position. Brush the working leg up to passé while rising onto the supporting leg's relevé. Hold the passé-relevé shape 3-5 seconds. Switch.

name: Chaînés Turn Prep (Spot Turns)
description: Linked turning prep with spotting — primary turn drill for multiple dance forms.
instructions_excerpt: Stand with feet together. Step and turn 180° in one direction, snapping the head quickly to maintain a focal spot. Step and turn another 180°. Continue in a line.

name: Frog Stretch (Adductor Opener)
description: Deep adductor stretch — essential mobility drill for dancers, gymnasts, movement athletes.
instructions_excerpt: On hands and knees, widen the knees as far as comfortable; shins parallel to each other. Lower hips back toward heels until you feel deep adductor stretch. Hold 60-90 seconds.

name: Reactive Start Drill
description: Start-on-cue explosive drill — handler-side speed for dog-agility and bikejoring starts.
instructions_excerpt: Stand in an athletic stance. On a partner's or timer's cue, explode into a 10-15 ft sprint or first stride. Reset and repeat. Short, quality reps only.

name: Alpine Start Warm-Up Flow
description: Full-body dynamic warm-up designed for cold-morning mountaineering starts.
instructions_excerpt: Cycle: 20 arm circles forward/back, 10 leg swings per side, 10 bodyweight squats, 10 walking lunges per side, 10 mountain climbers, 10 inchworms. Repeat 2 rounds. 5-8 minutes.

name: Track Sprint Build 60s
description: Progressive 60 m sprint — primary masters-sprint neuromuscular session.
instructions_excerpt: Build from 50% to ~90% effort across 60 m. Walk back recovery. 6-10 reps.

name: Race-Pace Strides
description: Short race-pace strides — speed maintenance for all running disciplines.
instructions_excerpt: After easy warm-up, run 6-10 strides of 80-100 m at race pace with full recovery between. Keep form relaxed.

name: Double-Foot Stomp Reset
description: Fast double-foot stomp + combat reset — neural primer for fencing/TKD/BJJ start positions.
instructions_excerpt: Stand in stance. Stomp both feet hard in place, simultaneously reset hands to guard. 10 reps. Rest 30s. 3 rounds.

name: Rider Core Plank with Reach
description: Plank with alternating arm reach — core stability for rein handling under motion.
instructions_excerpt: From a push-up plank, slowly reach one arm forward, return, switch. 8 per side. Keep hips square and level.

name: Senior-Friendly Golf Mobility Warmup
description: Short mobility warm-up for 55+ golfers — hip, thoracic, shoulder prep with no load.
instructions_excerpt: Cycle: 5 hip circles per side, 5 arm circles forward / back, 5 torso rotations, 5 bodyweight squats. 2 rounds.

name: Static Balance with Rifle/Bow Mount
description: Static single-leg balance while holding a rifle/bow mount — real-hunt prep.
instructions_excerpt: Stand on one leg in a soft shoe. Mount a rifle or bow (or PVC). Hold 30-45s. Switch.

name: Beach-Tennis Lateral Lunge Drill
description: Low lateral lunges + racquet swings — beach-tennis and paddle footwork.
instructions_excerpt: Step into a deep lateral lunge, swing racquet across. Reset, other side. 10 per side.

name: Swing-Dance Triple-Step Drill
description: Rhythmic triple-step pattern at musical tempo — swing-dance and lindy hop specific.
instructions_excerpt: Triple-step (step-step-step) right, triple-step left in swing rhythm. 2-3 min continuous with breaks.

name: Kung-Fu Crane Balance
description: One-leg crane stance hold — foundational kung-fu balance pose.
instructions_excerpt: Stand on one leg, opposite knee lifted, opposite arm raised in crane beak. Hold 20-45s per side.

name: Dressage Seated Balance Iso
description: Seated balance-ball hold in dressage posture — rider seat stability.
instructions_excerpt: Sit on a stability ball in dressage posture (shoulders-hip-heel aligned, tall spine). Hold 60-120s without feet touching.
